data.name: Elbert
data.gender_notes: Elbert is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old High German name Elbero, which can be broken down into 'elf' and 'bright'. The name Elbert was popular in Europe during the Middle Ages and was given to boys born into noble families. The name Elbert carries the meaning “Elf-bright or noble elf” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Elbert usually hope their child will grow to embody elf-bright or noble elf and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.long_meaning: Ελβέρτης είναι ένα όνομα γερμανικής προέλευσης που σημαίνει 'ευγενής λαμπρός' ή 'λαμπρός ευγενής'. Στην ελληνική παράδοση, το όνομα Ελβέρτης έχει συσχετιστεί με την έννοια της φωτεινότητας και της πνευματικής καθαρότητας, αντανακλώντας τις αξίες της χριστιανικής πίστης.

in_latin.name: Elbertus
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Elbertus origine germanica ortum est et componitur ex 'æl', quod significat Deus, et 'bert', quod significat clarus seu illustris. In traditione christiana, nomen Elbertus habetur ut symbolum fortitudinis et luminis, exprimens valores fundamentales fidei christianae.

in_english.name: Elbert
in_english.meaning: Elbert means bright noble or shining light
in_english.long_meaning: The name Elbert originates from Germanic roots, specifically from 'Adalbert', which is composed of 'adal', meaning noble, and 'bert', meaning bright or famous. In Christian tradition, Elbert signifies a person of noble character and shining light, embodying virtues of leadership, wisdom, and spiritual illumination. Historically, the name Elbert has been borne by several notable figures, including saints and nobles, underscoring its significance in Christian culture.

data.cultural_impact: Elbert was a name of nobility and honor in medieval Europe. It signified power, strength, and virtue, making it an ideal name for a son of nobility. The name Elbert continued to be popular during the colonization of America, and many early settlers gave the name to their children as a mark of their heritage.
